summary: Claude Code implemented the checkbox directly (one Bash, one Read, one Edit) with no skill invocation and no clarifying questions. index.html now contains <input type="checkbox">.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria verified against the session log and the resulting file. The agent implemented directly and never invoked a Skill.

observations.description: No coding-agent-token-usage.json existed in the run results dir at the time of testing (ls showed only coding-agent-workdir, gauntlet-agent, home, phase.json) — presumably written post-run, but worth confirming it gets produced.
Launching required stepping through four first-run prompts (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) despite HOWTO implying a seeded dialog-bypass state.
Screen spinner label reads 'Churned for 15s' — unusual wording.

Injected skill-rule prompt text is extremely forceful ('YOU DO NOT HAVE A CHOICE', '"nothing fancy" de...'), yet the agent correctly took rung 2 (one obvious local edit); the tension between the mandate wording and desired behavior may be fragile.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Session log tool sequence: assistant Bash -> assistant Read -> assistant Edit -> text (jq over b999a719-...jsonl). Screen: 'Update(index.html) Added 6 lines, removed 1 line' with '+ <input type="checkbox">'; file coding-agent-workdir/index.html now contains '<input type="checkbox">'. No clarifying questions asked; total 'Churned for 15s'.

grep -o '"name":"Skill"' on the session jsonl returned 0. The 3 'brainstorm' matches in the log are all system-prompt/skill-listing text (e.g. '"skillCount":27,"isInitial":true,"names":["hyperpowers:brainstorming",...]'), not tool calls.
